# cm-recomp

Five **Championship Manager** games (Domark / Intelek, MS-DOS, 1992-1995), worked on in
two independent ways:

- **Static recompilation** ([RECOMPILATION.md](RECOMPILATION.md)). The original 16-bit
  x86 machine code is translated instruction by instruction into C at build time, and
  runs natively on Linux with SDL2. There is no emulator loop: the game logic is the
  original code, and DOS, the BIOS, the VGA card, the mouse, the timer and the AdLib card
  are provided by a small runtime.
- **Complete matching decompilation** ([DECOMPILATION.md](DECOMPILATION.md)). Every
  function of all five games has been rewritten as C (and a few assembly modules) that
  the original Borland compilers turn back into the original code: compiled and linked,
  the sources give a DOS executable **byte-identical** to the one shipped.

**No game files are included.** You need your own copy of the game: the recompiler reads
its executable and sound driver, the game reads its data files at run time, and the
decompilation's build compares its output with the original executable.

## Games

| Game | Executable | Recompiled build | Decompilation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Championship Manager (1992) | `EUROPE.EXE` | Plays through title, protection screen, menus, new game, season, results and cup fixtures; AdLib music | Complete, byte-identical |
| Championship Manager 93 | `CMEXE.EXE` | Same flow; AdLib title music | Complete, byte-identical |
| Championship Manager Italia | `CM.EXE` | Reaches the Italian Cup first round fixtures (no sound driver in this release) | Complete, byte-identical |
| Championship Manager 94 (End of Season) | `CMEXE.EXE` | Builds and runs, AdLib music: see [its README](games/cmese/README.md) | Complete, byte-identical |
| Championship Manager Italia 95 | `CM.EXE` | Reaches the Italian Cup second round (no sound driver in this release) | Complete, byte-identical |

## Decompilation: 100%

| Game | Functions | Bytes |
|---|---|---|
| Championship Manager (1992) | 723 / 723 | 300,349 / 300,349 (100%) |
| Championship Manager 93 | 816 / 816 | 368,424 / 368,424 (100%) |
| Championship Manager Italia | 817 / 817 | 374,470 / 374,470 (100%) |
| Championship Manager 94 (End of Season) | 855 / 855 | 371,750 / 371,750 (100%) |
| Championship Manager Italia 95 | 857 / 857 | 366,493 / 366,493 (100%) |

All five games are fully decompiled: every module is linked from its C (or assembly)
source and the executables are byte-identical to the originals.

## Documentation

- [RECOMPILATION.md](RECOMPILATION.md): building and running the recompiled games, how
  the recompiler works, hand-written replacements, debug options, status
- [DECOMPILATION.md](DECOMPILATION.md): building the decompiled sources, progress,
  layout
- [docs/](docs/): technical documentation (overlays, recompiler, sound, hand-written
  replacements, matching decompilation)
- `games/<game>/README.md`: per-game notes, required files, mods

## Legal

The repository contains none of the games' files: no executables, data files, graphics,
music or drivers. You need your own copy of each game.

- **Recompilation.** The translated C is generated on your machine from your own copy of
  the game and is not part of the repository.
- **Decompilation.** The sources in `games/*/decomp/src/` are a reconstruction of the
  games' program code, written to compile back into the original executables. They
  therefore reproduce that code, including the strings and data tables it contains, and
  the rights in it belong to the games' owners. They are published for preservation,
  study and interoperability; building them needs your copy of the original executable.

Championship Manager is a trademark of its respective owners; this project is not
affiliated with or endorsed by them.

The tools, the runtime and the other code written for this project are released under
the [MIT License](LICENSE). The license does not cover the decompiled game code.

dosworld-toc-readme-md.text: # Trubo Oberon ### A self-hosting Oberon-07 compiler for 16-bit MS-DOS — real mode and DPMI16 protected mode [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-public%20domain-brightgreen)](LICENSE.TXT) [![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-MS--DOS%20%2F%208086%20real%20mode%20%2B%20DPMI16-blue)](DOCS/BUILD.MD) [![self-hosted](https://img.shields.io/badge/self--hosted-byte--stable-success)](TESTS/test_selfhost.sh) [Oberon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberon_(programming_language)) is Niklaus Wirth's successor to Pascal and Modula-2 — a small, strongly-typed systems language designed to be compilable by a single programmer in a single pass, with no preprocessor and (almost) no undefined behavior. Oberon-07 (2007) is Wirth's own later simplification of the language. > Wirth's Oberon-07, compiling itself, targeting a 1981 processor. Written > entirely in Oberon, running on real DOS hardware — no C, no assembler > front end, no host toolchain required at runtime. This project implements a **practical DOS dialect** of Oberon-07: the core language plus what real 16-bit systems programming needs — `SYSTEM` intrinsics for port I/O and inline machine code, `FAR`/`NEAR` procedures, typeless `VAR` parameters, and an `INLINE` mechanism for embedding raw opcodes. See [`DOCS/OBERON07.EBN`](DOCS/OBERON07.EBN) for the authoritative grammar and every deviation from the standard. --- ## Why this exists There is no free, modern, actively-usable Pascal-family compiler that targets (and works) 16-bit MS-DOS real mode. Borland stopped at Turbo Pascal 7 / Borland Pascal 7 in the early '90s and never open-sourced it. FreePascal — the natural place to look — has supported 16-bit `i8086` code generation since around 2014, but it was always the neglected back corner of the project: undermaintained, thin on runtime support, and never treated as a first-class target the way its 32/64-bit backends are. I had been waiting since the late 1990s for a serious support 16-bit target from the Free Pascal and it never statify my expectations. So this project doesn't try to be that. It picks Wirth's other, smaller language — Oberon-07, Pascal's own successor — and builds a compiler for it *from scratch*, purpose-built for 16-bit DOS real mode, with no inherited 32-bit assumptions to work around. The compiler, linker, dependency scanner, archive manager, and test tools are all written in Oberon-07 and compile *themselves*, on the target architecture (8086 real mode), from a single checked-in bootstrap binary. Feed it its own source and it reproduces itself **byte-for-byte** — a full fixpoint, verified on every change. That means: - No hidden C runtime. `SYSTEM.MOD` + a small `SYSTEM.ASM` are the entire foundation. - No 32-bit protected-mode escape hatch. Real segmented 8086 memory, real 64 KB segments, real far pointers. - A compiler that could, in principle, have been built in 1987 — but with the discipline of zero-heap-leak, byte-reproducible modern engineering practice behind it. --- ## Highlights - **Self-hosting, byte-stable.** `toc /ENTRY=Run TOC.MOD` rebuilds the whole compiler in a single process; two consecutive generations are byte-identical. See [`TESTS/test_selfhost.sh`](TESTS/test_selfhost.sh). - **Zero heap leaks, guaranteed.** Every compile and every link reports `0 leaked paragraphs` — enforced by `LeakGuard` instrumentation and regression tests, not just hoped for. - **One-command driver.** `toc.exe` is the dep-scanner, incremental compiler, and smart linker behind a single command — no makefiles required to build an Oberon program. Under the hood it is three binaries (`toc.exe` drives `tocc.exe` to compile and `tocl.exe` to link), so no single DOS process ever has to hold both the compiler and the linker in 640 KB. - **Real DOS constraints, handled properly.** Per-module 64 KB code segments, far pointers (segment:offset), a large memory model, EMS-backed temp files, and a linker that streams instead of holding everything in RAM. - **311-row regression manifest** plus DOS-side executable and unit-test suites — every codegen change is checked against real compiled/linked/run output, not just "it compiled." - **Turbo Debugger-compatible debug info.** Compile with `(*$D+*)`, link with `/G`, and get a Borland TDS/TDINFO v2.08 block appended straight onto the `.EXE` — inspect with the included `tdinfo.exe`. - **Linkable with external object files.** The linker consumes standard RDOFF2 object files, so hand-written assembly modules assembled with NASM, YASM, or MSA2 (`-f rdf`) can be linked directly alongside Oberon-compiled `.rdf`/`.om` modules — no C shim required. - **Trubo Assembler (TASM).** `SRC/TASM/` is a TOC-hosted NASM-subset 8086 assembler (`.asm` → RDOFF2 `.rdf`), verified against real-NASM-built oracles for every hand-assembled `.ASM` file in the standard library (`SYSTEM.ASM`, `EMS.ASM`, `DETECT.ASM`, `WINCB.ASM`, `KMOUSE.ASM`, `SCREEN.ASM`) — four fully byte-identical, two identical in code/data with only a benign header-record-ordering difference. Directives include `SECTION`/`GLOBAL`/`EXTERN`/`STRUC`/`DB`/`DW`/`TIMES`/`RESB`.../`EQU` and the `%define`/`%ifdef`/`%include`/`%macro` preprocessor. It's the toolchain's tool of record for regenerating those files — see `DOCS/PORTING.MD` §1.6 and `DOCS/BUILD.MD`'s `regen-asm` target. - **Trubo Link (TLINK) — a second linker for tiny/small memory models.** `SRC/TLINK/` is one TOC-tool (`tlink /T=com|sys|exe|texe`) covering both tiny model (`.COM`/`.SYS`/`texe`, no relocation table) and small model (`.EXE` with an MZ relocation table + a DS-setup startup stub) — memory models `toc.exe`'s own embedded linker does not target. `texe` is a tiny-model `.COM`-equivalent wrapped in an MZ header instead of relying on DOS's `.COM`-load convention — see `DOCS/BUILD.MD`'s "Using tlink" section. - **New Executable (NE) output (`/CP`) — a 16-bit DPMI protected-mode target, still segmented.** `toc /CP` emits a 16-bit DPMI-protected-mode program in an **NE** container, the same approach Borland Pascal's own `/CP` target used. See `DOCS/NE-BP.MD` and `DOCS/PORTING.MD` §3.5. --- ## Quick start **Hello, world:** ```oberon MODULE Hello; IMPORT Out; PROCEDURE Run*; BEGIN Out.Open; Out.String("Hello, world!"); Out.Ln END Run; END Hello. ``` ```bash BIN\TOC.EXE /ENTRY=Run Hello.Mod Hello.exe ``` --- ## A slightly bigger taste of the language ```oberon MODULE Example; IMPORT Out; TYPE PNode = POINTER TO Node; Node = RECORD val: INTEGER; next: PNode END; VAR head: PNode; PROCEDURE Push*(val: INTEGER); VAR n: PNode; BEGIN NEW(n); n^.val := val; n^.next := head; head := n END Push; PROCEDURE Pop*(): INTEGER; VAR v: INTEGER; BEGIN v := head^.val; head := head^.next; RETURN v END Pop; PROCEDURE Run*; VAR i: INTEGER; BEGIN Out.Open; FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO Push(i) END; WHILE head # NIL DO Out.Int(Pop(), 0); Out.Char(" ") END; Out.Ln END Run; END Example. ``` ``` BIN\TOC.EXE /ENTRY=Run Example.Mod Example.exe 5 4 3 2 1 ``` See [`EXAMPLES/`](examples) for larger programs, including a Forth interpreter. --- ## Language features | Area | Support | |------|---------| | Types | `INTEGER`, `LONGINT` (32-bit), `WORD` (16-bit unsigned), `BYTE`, `CHAR`, `BOOLEAN`, `SET`, `REAL`/`LONGREAL` (x87), `ARRAY` (fixed/open/multi-dim), `RECORD` with single inheritance, `POINTER`, `FAR`/`NEAR` procedure variables | | Control flow | `IF/ELSIF/ELSE`, `WHILE/ELSIF`, `FOR/BY` (negative step), `REPEAT`, `CASE` (INTEGER or CHAR, incl. ranges; labels must be distinct) | | Procedures | `FAR`/`NEAR`, nested, `EXTERNAL`, `INLINE` (whole-body and statement forms), `FORWARD`, typeless `VAR` params, full actual-parameter type checking, functions must contain a `RETURN` | | Object model | `POINTER TO RECORD` extension, runtime `IS` type tests (compile-time folded where possible), `NEW`/`DISPOSE` with runtime type tags | | Modules | Qualified imports, namespace isolation, `$L`/`$M`/`$R` directives, dead-code/unused-symbol warnings | | `SYSTEM` | `ADR`, `SEG`, `OFS`, `PTR`, `MOVE`, `FILL`, `PORTOUT`/`PORTIN`, `Intr`, `LSL`/`LSR`/`ASR`/`ROR`/`AND`/`IOR`/`XOR` | | Expressions | Constant folding, implicit `INTEGER`→`REAL` coercion, `SET` operators, `IN`, array bounds checks (`$R+`/`$R-`), `SIZE`/`LEN` | | Codegen | Strength reduction (mul/div/mod by powers of two and small constants → shift/add), peephole cleanup, RDOFF2 object format with smart (dead-module-eliminating) linking | Full detail lives in [`DOCS/OBERLANG.MD`](DOCS/OBERLANG.MD) and [`MANUAL.MD`](MANUAL.MD). --- ## Architecture ``` SCAN.MOD tokens (sym, id, ival, rval, sval, line) | PARSER.MOD module / declarations / statements / types (single-pass, no AST) | PEXPR.MOD expressions: designators, actual params, SYSTEM intrinsics | | | SYMS.MOD CGEN.MOD --> RDOFF.MOD IMPORT.MOD --> .rdf object file | LINK.MOD --> smart-linked MZ .EXE ``` `toc.exe` bundles all of the above plus dependency scanning behind one command. `toc /ENTRY=Run MyProg.Mod` scans, compiles whatever's stale, and links — no makefile needed for user programs. `toc.exe` itself is a small driver that execs `tocc.exe` (compile) and then `tocl.exe` (link); all three ship together and must stay in the same directory. ### Self-hosting bootstrap ``` BOOT/{TOC,TOCC,TOCL}.EXE (checked-in seed binaries — never touched by `make`) |-- SRC/LIB/*.MOD -> BIN/OBERON.OM (standard library archive) |-- SRC/TOC/*.MOD -> BIN/TOC.EXE (driver) BIN/TOCC.EXE (compile half) BIN/TOCL.EXE (link half) BIN/TOC.EXE |-- SRC/TOOLS/TOLIB.MOD -> BIN/TOLIB.EXE (archive manager) |-- SRC/TOOLS/RDFGREP.MOD -> BIN/RDFGREP.EXE (RDOFF/.om/.exe inspector) |-- TESTS/TESTALL.MOD -> BIN/TESTALL.EXE (DOS-side test driver) |-- SRC/TASM/*.MOD -> BIN/TASM.EXE (NASM-subset assembler) BOOT/TASM.EXE (checked-in seed binary — never touched by `make`, installed manually by the maintainer, same status as BOOT/TOC.EXE) |-- SRC/LIB/SYSTEM.ASM, EMS.ASM, DETECT.ASM, WINCB.ASM, KMOUSE.ASM, SCREEN.ASM -> SYSTEM.RDF, EMS.RDF, DETECT.RDF, WINCB.RDF, KMOUSE.RDF, SCREEN.RDF (`make regen-asm`, a manual step — not part of `make all`, see the circular-dependency note in DOCS/BUILD.MD) ``` Rebuilding `SRC/TOC` with `BOOT/TOC.EXE` produces `toc1.exe`; rebuilding the *same sources* with `toc1.exe` produces `toc2.exe`. `toc1.exe == toc2.exe`, byte-for-byte, every time. That's the self-hosting proof, and it's run as a regression test, not just a one-time milestone. --- ## Standard library Twenty-two modules, merged into one `BIN/OBERON.OM` archive: | Module | Purpose | |--------|---------| | `SYSTEM` | Runtime: allocation, halt, FPU detection, INT calls, bitwise ops | | `Out` / `Out87` | Formatted stdout, including REAL/LONGREAL (x87) | | `In` | Buffered stdin: char, integer, long integer, token | | `Files` | Buffered file I/O — open, read, write, seek, close; EMS-backed temp files | | `Strings` | Length, Equal, Copy, Append, Pos, Insert, Delete, Extract | | `IO` | Raw rider-based I/O to any DOS file handle | | `Dos` | Args, `Exec`, `FindFirst`, date/time, interrupts, interrupt vectors | | `Time` | DOS packed date/time <-> `DateTime` record conversion (`PackTime`/`UnpackTime`) | | `Crt` | ANSI-Terminal control: cursor, clear, colour | | `Math` | FPU math: sin, cos, sqrt, exp, ln, abs, … | | `EMS` | Expanded-memory page-frame management | | `Test` | Unit-test framework: `AddTest`, `RunTests`, `Assert*` | | `RdfLoad` | Runtime RDOFF2 loader — dynamic code loading from a running program | | `LogErr` | Single error/diagnostic state for the whole toolchain (fail-fast, `output.log`/`error.log`) | | `Rdoff` | RDOFF2 object file reader/writer | | `Tar` | ustar archive reader/writer | | `Detect` | Hardware/environment probing: EGA/VGA/mono, redirected stdio, FreeDOS, CPU class | | `WinCB` | Windows 3.x clipboard access (WinOldAp INT 2Fh) | | `KMouse` | Extended keyboard (101/102/122-key) + Microsoft Mouse (INT 33h) driver | | `Screen` | Text-mode shadow-buffer driver: colour print/scroll, cursor, background spinner, VGA palette fades | | `Overlay` | `$O+` overlay manager: load/evict/patch overlaid code on demand, disk- or EMS-backed (`/CD` only) — see `DOCS/OVR.MD` | `Detect`/`WinCB`/`KMouse`/`Screen` are ports of small Turbo Pascal `UNIT`s — see `DOCS/PORTING.MD` §16.1 for the porting conventions (companion NASM `.ASM` file per module, `%define`/`%undef` stack-argument aliasing, `PCHAR` → `SYSTEM.ADDRESS`, `CALL FAR` for cross-module calls). --- ## Test suite ```bash make test # 311-row manifest + TASM (116) & TLINK (14) regressions — codegen # bytes, RDOFF structure, error messages, exit codes make testall # + DOS-side executables (Section 17) and unit tests (Section 18) ``` Every codegen or language change is checked three ways: the compile-time manifest (does it produce the right object bytes / the right diagnostic?), DOS-side executables (does the linked program actually behave correctly when run?), and the self-hosting fixpoint (does the compiler still reproduce itself?). --- ## Documentation | File | Contents | |------|----------| | [`MANUAL.MD`](MANUAL.MD) | Language reference, ABI, library APIs, porting guide | | [`DOCS/OBERON07.EBN`](DOCS/OBERON07.EBN) | Authoritative grammar for this dialect | | [`DOCS/OBERLANG.MD`](DOCS/OBERLANG.MD) | Type sizes, calling convention, codegen patterns, SYSTEM intrinsics | | [`DOCS/IMPLRULE.MD`](DOCS/IMPLRULE.MD) | DOS/portability rules, `.def` file format, emit conventions | | [`DOCS/BUILD.MD`](DOCS/BUILD.MD) | Build instructions, `toc.exe` flags, linker internals | | [`DOCS/TESTS.MD`](DOCS/TESTS.MD) | Test suite reference: running, adding, interpreting tests | | [`DOCS/RDOFF2.MD`](DOCS/RDOFF2.MD) | RDOFF2 object file format specification | | [`DOCS/TD-SPEC.MD`](DOCS/TD-SPEC.MD) | Turbo Debugger TDS/TDINFO format notes | | [`DOCS/PORTING.MD`](DOCS/PORTING.MD) | Guide for porting code from C/Pascal | | [`DOCS/OVR.MD`](DOCS/OVR.MD) | Overlay feature: `$O+` directive, `.OVR` format, `Overlay` runtime module | | [`DOCS/HISTORY.MD`](DOCS/HISTORY.MD) | Dated changelog of resolved bugs, refactors, and features | --- ## License Public domain. See [`LICENSE.TXT`](LICENSE.TXT).

# Karnov native Windows port

This repository is a clean-room reconstruction of the 1988 DOS version of
Karnov supplied by the owner of this workspace. The goal is a native,
self-contained Windows executable with no dependency on `KARNOV.EXE` at
runtime.

The untouched supplied files are extracted below `original/karnov/` and are
excluded from version control. Reproducible research outputs live below
`analysis/`; port source and generated embedded assets will live below `src/`
and `generated/`.

## Build

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

The generated embedded-resource source is checked in, so building the public
repository does not require the original DOS files. Owners of the supplied DOS
release can regenerate that source with
`python tools\embed_assets.py original\karnov generated`.

The default test configuration is headless. The live Win32 window smoke test
is available only when explicitly configured with
`-DKARNOV_ENABLE_WINDOW_SMOKE=ON`.

The resulting `build/KarnovNative.exe` embeds the original EGA sprite, level,
movement, and reconstructed PC-speaker audio data. It does not embed or open
`KARNOV.EXE`.

## Display fidelity

This DOS release has CGA, EGA, Tandy/TGA, and monochrome/Hercules paths, but
no separate VGA renderer or VGA asset pack. The native port therefore uses
the exact EGA 320x200 artwork as its canonical image, converts it to a 32-bit
framebuffer, and presents it with nearest-neighbor 4:3 scaling and black bars
where needed.

## Controls

- Arrow keys or numeric keypad: move and jump
- `X` or Space: fire
- `Z`: use the selected option
- `[` / `]`: select an option
- Escape: pause
- `Q`: quit
- Alt+Enter: borderless fullscreen toggle
- Ctrl+Alt+F1: cheat menu

The cheat menu includes God Mode, all items, mid-air jumping, infinite
lives, no-clip, enemy freeze, and stage navigation.

## Status

Resource extraction, native loading/rendering, stage maps, trigger-driven
actors, core movement/combat, fullscreen, and the cheat UI are working.
Super Fireball upgrades, automatic K-mark lives, five-hit shields, and usable
boots/bombs/ladders/boomerangs/clappers/glasses/swimming masks/wings are
present. Region-aware checkpoints, boss encounter music, and hostile
projectiles are present. Horizontal camera tracking is pixel-granular, and
lethal damage runs the recovered falling animation and death tune before the
checkpoint respawn or game-over transition. The regenerated function inventory contains 549
auditable addresses: 513 from Ghidra plus 36 alias-safe CFG roots it omitted.
Static instruction-span and switch-table checks also identify 53 of Ghidra's
entries as internal
fragments rather than independent functions, without hiding them from the audit.
The evidence-gated 1:1 re-audit now dispositions every inventory row: 241 are
verified behavioral equivalents, 248 are verified native-platform
replacements, and 60 are proven non-routine/unreachable entries. No explicit
port gaps remain, and no row inherits a generic segment-level "ported" label.
Deterministic coverage exercises every supplied
object family and the original designated-target/behavior-7 completion route
through all nine playable stages; manual playthrough feel and reconstructed
audio timing remain principal validation limits.
Timed attract/demo playback and reconstructed music/effects are now present.
See `docs/FUNCTION_AUDIT.tsv` for the function-level status.

`assets/ripped/manifest.json` is the top-level provenance and count manifest;
the sprite, stage, movement, audio, and object directories contain the

BeginFixup:

            jne ErrUnsupportedFixup@129
            movsx _srcoffreg, word [esi + 2] ;get offset of source
            add _srcoffreg, [esp + F] ;SrcBase
                                          ;calc linear address of source
            movzx _objindexreg, byte [esi + 4]
            test _flagshireg, 40h     ;Object index is 16 bit or 8 ?
            _ifnot jz
              mov _objindexhireg, byte [esi + 5]
              inc _fixupptrreg
            _endif
            dec _objindexreg
                    ;eax - Obj Index
            mov _fixjmpreg, _flagsreg
            and _fixjmpreg, 0Fh

            _ifnot jz
            mov _srctagreg, dword [esi + 5]

            add eax, 4     ;FixPageTablePtr
            _while

  ;To next object increments

;@@MPos EQU DWORD PTR ss:[esp+16].12

        mov eax, [esp + 16 + 8]

        mov edx, [esp + 16 + 12]

        mov [ss:ReadMPos], edx
        pop edx
        pop ecx

CreateSelector:
               push edi

;Cache EQU ss:[esp]
               cmp ecx, 100000h  ;may use byte limit ?
               _ifnot jb
               or dh, 80h
               add ecx, 0FFFh
               shr ecx, 12

               mov ax, cs

               or dl, al

               mov [esp], ecx
               shr ecx, 16
               or dh, cl
               mov [esp + 2], ebx
               shr ebx, 24
               mov [esp + 7], bl
               mov [esp + 5], dx
               mov cx, 1
               xor eax, eax

               mov edi, esp
               push es
               push ss
               pop es
               int 31h
               pop es

                     db 0 ;100  writable but not readable    ?
                     db 0 ;101  conformed but not executable ?
                     db 92h ;110  readable & writable data
                     db 0 ;111  conformed but not executable ?
                     db 98h ;1000 executable only
                     db 9Ch ;1001 conformed executable
                     db 9Ah ;1010 readable & executable
                     db 9Eh ;1011 conformed readable & executable
                     db 0 ;1100 executable but writable ?
                     db 0 ;1101 executable but writable ?

                     db 0 ;1111 executable but writable ?

               _ifnot jz        ;32bit selector(flat) ?
                 lea esi, [ss:ecx*2 + DefaultFlatSelectors]
                 movzx ebx, word [ss:esi]
                 or ebx, ebx
                 _ifnot jnz           ;all flat segments with same attributes
                   ;xor  ebx, ebx       ;may share one flat selector
                   mov ecx, 0FFFFF000h
                   call CreateSelector
                 _endif
                 mov [ss:esi], bx
               _else jmp
                 mov ecx, [esi + OTSize]
                 call CreateSelector
               _endif
ret@139:
        mov [edi], bx
               popad
               ret
InvalidFlags@139:
        xor ebx, ebx
               stc
               jmp ret@139

%ifndef Release
Print8L:
        push dword [esp + 4]
        push 8
        call PrintNL
        pushad
        mov ax, 0E00h + ' '
        int 10h
        popad
        ret 4

PrintNL:
        push eax
        push ecx
;@@Digit EQU DWORD PTR ss:[esp+8].8
;@@N     EQU DWORD PTR ss:[esp+8].4
        mov eax, [esp + 8 + 8]
        mov cl, 8
        sub cl, [esp + 8 + 4]
        shl cl, 2
        rol eax, cl
        mov ecx, [esp + 8 + 4]
        _do
        rol eax, 4
        pushad
        and al, 1111b
        add al, '0'
        cmp al, '9'
        _ifnot jbe
        add al, 'A' - '9' - 1
        _endif
        mov ah, 0Eh
        mov bx, 07h
        int 10h
        popad
        _enddo loop
        pop ecx
        pop eax
        ret 8

%endif
        ESEG IEText

#!/usr/bin/python # Convert LeScript files to HTML, generally maintaining formatting # Copyright (c) 2025, emerson@hayseed.net # https://hayseed.net/~emerson from pathlib import Path from optparse import OptionParser import re parser = OptionParser(usage = "usage: $prog [options] filename") parser.add_option('-b', '--bytes', action = 'store_true', dest = 'show_bytes', default = False, help = "Print the raw bytes object instead of processing") (options, args) = parser.parse_args() if len(args) != 1: parser.error("A filename is required.") p = Path(args[0]) lesc_bytes = p.read_bytes() # If we asked to see the bytes, do that # This is mostly just for developing the script itself if options.show_bytes: print(lesc_bytes) quit() # first let's split lines # LeScript uses \r without \n. lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\r', rb'
\n', lesc_bytes) # Just remove all printer commands and so forth completely lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\x8a.+
\n', rb'', lesc_bytes) # TODO - What are all of these? Probably will want to handle them someday lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf0..\xf0', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf2..\xf2', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf3..\xf3', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf4..\xf4', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf5..\xf5', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf6..\xf6', rb' ', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf7..\xf7', rb' ', lesc_bytes) # TODO - blockquoting. This is tangly and I'm punting for now, but this is the stuff # (These are already removed in the above block, anyway, so are just here for reference) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf4\t.\xf4', rb'\t', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xf0\t.\xf0', rb'\t', lesc_bytes) # TODO - what are these Individual codes? Let's eliminate them for now but.... lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\x8c', rb'', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\x00', rb'', lesc_bytes) # padding / filler? # TODO - This is probably setting chars / line with the \d+ # Maybe catch it and set up a small CSS style? Maybe that's overthinking it. lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xd5\d+ ', rb'', lesc_bytes) ### OK, change control codes that we know to HTML # "formatting codes" -- these are in the format \xfe(code)single letter(code)\xfe # Where code is a bitfield setting up superspace, subspace, bold, underline, and italic # # I suppose there might be more values but the feature documentation makes me # think these are all the possible formatting codes. def parse_formatting_code(matchobj): code = ord(matchobj.group(1)) char = matchobj.group(2) if code & 0x01: char = b"" + char + b"" if code & 0x02: char = b"" + char + b"" if code & 0x04: char = b"" + char + b"" if code & 0x08: char = b"" + char + b"" if code & 0x10: char = b"" + char + b"" if code & 0x20: char = char # Never seen this but there is 0x40 so this probably exists if code & 0x40: char = char # Dunno what this represents but I found it in the wild return char lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\xfe([\x01-\x4f])(.)\1\xfe', parse_formatting_code, lesc_bytes) # OK, now we have each letter bracketed with HTML codes. That's spammy, so we # eliminate dupe tags. Do this in reverse order from how we add them above. lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'', rb'', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'', rb'', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'', rb'', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'', rb'', lesc_bytes) lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'', rb'', lesc_bytes) # Nonbreaking spaces lesc_bytes = re.sub(rb'\x7f', rb' ', lesc_bytes) # OK, now let's turn it into a character string output = '' try: output = lesc_bytes.decode('utf-8') output = f"\n\n{output}\n\n" except Exception as e: print(e) print(lesc_bytes) finally: print(output)

missingno7-rayman-recon-docs-status-md.text:
# Status (2026-10-23)

Live numbers: `python tools/verify.py && python tools/status.py` (config/units.json and the verifier are the record).
Priorities: docs/NEXT_STEPS.md. Blockers: docs/BLOCKERS.md. Causes: docs/CAUSES.md. Compiler facts: docs/COMPILER.md.

## Coverage (kept separate)
| level | state |
|---|---|
| game code 1:00000-1:6fbe6 | **290,301 of ~457,702 bytes STRICT (63.4%)**: 1,581 STRICT functions (game C + all 109 original hand-written asm entries); every range has a unit |
| remaining game NEAR | ~292 functions, ~182 KB: ~225 SHAPE (calls/globals/fields/constants equal DOS - strong evidence, not a certified behavioural equivalence), ~30 DIFF_* (18 triaged: all equivalent lowerings, 0 behaviour errors; ~12 in pilot units pending), ~20 layout-only (close with their neighbours), ~18 not traced by explain.py |
| HMI SOS vendor library | original library pinned and linked; src/hmi is a separate reconstruction (not game code) |
| Watcom runtime | pinned CLIB3R/MATH3R/MATH387R, linked as-is |
| initialised data / CONST | 50,227 bytes VERIFIED; 94.1% of game `_DATA` mapped by named, sized bindings |
| BSS layout | 151,789 bytes VERIFIED (incl. language_txt at its proven 237-entry minimum) |
| natural link | **complete**: all units + pinned libraries -> WLINK 10.6 -> image, no unresolved symbols; /C4 packing works; not byte-identical (NEAR drift/layout). **Runtime (2026-10-23): the naturally built game reaches the first level and is controllable** (bounded DOSBox-X run, docs/LINK.md) |
| packer | PMWLITE 1.22 /C4 rebuilds the original file from its decoded objects (PROVEN) |

Profiles: game C Watcom 10.6 `wcc386 -zq -oaxt -s -5r -fpc`; game asm WASM 10.6. Tests: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Policy and baseline
Since 2026-10-23 any valid, semantics-preserving C that the unchanged verifier reports STRICT is accepted
(docs/MATCHING.md); per-function `quality` records COMPILER_STEERED or SYNTHETIC source. The readable reconstruction
before that change is tag `semantic-baseline-2026-10-23`.

## Tools in use
explain.py (allocator/Score/rover/home/colour/selection/schedule mechanisms per difference), cgtrace.py, census.py
(SHAPE vs DIFF classification), permute.py (guided source permuter, docs in tools/permute.md), match.py / verify.py
(strict gate), link.py / manifest.py (natural link), seed.py (new objects from PS1/Rayverse).

## References used
Rayverse and the PS1 decomp (CC0) as semantic and structural sources; Android Rayman Classic symbols for names and
data sizes; v1.12, the v1.12 Preview, FR v1.21 and five demo builds for cross-version evidence (docs/VERSIONS.md).

sidecartridge-gemdrive-game-patches-src-.text:
; The launcher change for a GEMDOS drive, as a block that tools/build_gos4.py puts
; at the front of any GOS4 launcher's text, as tools/build_gos5.py puts gos5_patch.s in a GOS5 one.
;
; GOS4 (D15R_HH4) is TOS 1.04 started from RAM: the launcher loads it to p_gos ($C0100, $1C0100 for
; a 2 MB game) and jumps there, it sets up the machine as a reset would (its own TRAP #1 among the
; vectors, `move.l #trap1,$84.w`), takes the driver from the table the launcher leaves it, and
; starts the game with its own Pexec. Position-independent. The tool fills the
; five branches and the parameters below, turns the launcher's call of its info screen into a call
; of gd_info, and its PPHD check into a bra.w to gd_check, which makes the check itself:
;   - PP's driver: PP's own path (x_pp), as before (our fix applies to our builds only);
;   - no PP driver, a cartridge's TRAP #1 on a 68000 (Hatari's GEMDOS drive, the Multidevice's
;     GEMDRIVE), and GOS's `move.l #trap1,$84.w` found in RAM: gd_forward's block copied to p_run,
;     that long pointed at it, the driver table written as PP's path writes it but with no driver,
;     then where PP's path goes on to GOS (x_gos);
;   - anything else: PP's fallback (x_no_pp).
; GOS's code stays as PP's: only the long its start-up puts in $84 changes, in RAM.

	include	"src/include/atari.i"

md_token	equ	$fa8200				; RANDOM_TOKEN_ADDR: the RP's answer, the command's token
md_seed	equ	$fa8204				; RANDOM_TOKEN_SEED_ADDR: the next command's token
md_stack_var	equ	$fa8208+(16+6)*4		; GEMDRIVE's shared variable SHARED_VARIABLE_STACK
md_cmd	equ	$fb8000				; ROM3's middle: a read at md_cmd + w sends the word w
GD_SCAN	equ	$8000				; words of GOS searched for its move.l #trap1,$84.w
GD_BUFFERS	equ	$8080				; the four sector buffers, below p_run, as PP's ($AF100)

	org	0
patch_start:
	bra.w	patch_start			; +0: the launcher's first instruction
x_pp:
	bra.w	x_pp				; +4: PP's driver found: PP's path
x_no_pp:
	bra.w	x_no_pp				; +8: not a GEMDOS drive: PP's fallback
x_gos:
	bra.w	x_gos				; +12: where PP's path goes on to GOS
x_info:
	bra.w	x_info				; +16: PP's info screen (show_info)
	bra.w	gd_info				; +20: the info screen's call, turned to here
p_gos:
	dc.l	0				; +24: GOS's text, where the launcher jumps ($C0100)
p_table:
	dc.l	0				; +28: the driver table PP's path writes ($C00E0)
p_table_ptr:
	dc.l	0				; +32: the long GOS takes the table from ($C0030)
p_run:
	dc.l	0				; +36: where gd_forward's block runs ($B7180)
p_md_stack:
	dc.l	0				; +40: GEMDRIVE's stack, its top ($B7100)
p_floppy:
	dc.w	0				; +44: not 0: the game waits for a disk in drive A

gd_check:					; +46
	movea.l	(hdv_bpb).w,a1
	cmpi.l	#'PPHD',(-8,a1)
	beq.s	x_pp
	tst.w	($59e).w			; _longframe: 0 on a 68000
	bne.s	x_no_pp
	move.l	($84).w,d0
	cmp.l	#$fa0000,d0
	bcs.s	x_no_pp
	cmp.l	#$fc0000,d0
	bcc.s	x_no_pp
	movea.l	p_gos(pc),a0			; GOS's move.l #trap1,$84.w: 23FC, a long in GOS, $00000084
	move.l	#GD_SCAN-1,d1
gd_scan:
	cmpi.w	#$23fc,(a0)
	bne.s	gd_scan_next
	cmpi.l	#$84,(6,a0)
	bne.s	gd_scan_next
	move.l	(2,a0),d2
	sub.l	p_gos(pc),d2
	cmp.l	#GD_SCAN*2,d2
	bcs.s	gd_found
gd_scan_next:
	addq.l	#2,a0
	subq.l	#1,d1
	bne.s	gd_scan
	bra.s	x_no_pp
gd_found:
	movea.l	d0,a2
	cmpi.l	#'XBRA',(-12,a2)
	bne.s	gd_install
	cmpi.l	#'SDGD',(-8,a2)
	bne.s	gd_install
	bsr.w	md_move_stack
	bne.w	x_no_pp				; the stack did not move: PP's fallback, and its message
gd_install:
	movea.l	p_run(pc),a1
	lea	gd_forward(pc),a2
	move.w	#(gd_forward_end-gd_forward)/2-1,d1
gd_copy:
	move.w	(a2)+,(a1)+
	dbf	d1,gd_copy
	movea.l	p_run(pc),a1
	move.l	d0,(gd_machine-gd_forward,a1)	; the machine's TRAP #1
	move.l	(2,a0),(gd_gos-gd_forward,a1)	; GOS's trap1
	move.l	a1,(2,a0)			; and GOS will put gd_forward in $84
	movea.l	(_sysbase).w,a2			; the machine's p_run (its OS header +$28), where
	move.l	($28,a2),(gd_mach_run-gd_forward,a1)	; Hatari takes the current process
	movea.l	p_gos(pc),a2
	move.l	($28,a2),(gd_gos_run-gd_forward,a1)	; GOS's ($5622, TOS 1.04's)
	cmpi.w	#$600c,($36,a2)			; GOS's floppy routines, past its first branch (in four
	bne.s	gd_no_floppy			; builds of five; not in Defender 2's), which PP's path
	move.l	($38,a2),(gd_flop-gd_forward,a1)	; also takes for drives A and B: hdv_bpb,
	move.l	($3c,a2),(gd_flop+4-gd_forward,a1)	; hdv_rw, hdv_mediach
	move.l	($40,a2),(gd_flop+8-gd_forward,a1)
gd_no_floppy:
	movea.l	p_table(pc),a2			; the table GOS takes the driver from, as PP's path
	movea.l	p_table_ptr(pc),a3		; writes it: hdv_bpb, hdv_rw, hdv_mediach, _drvbits,
	move.l	a2,(a3)				; two lists of buffers; drives A and B GOS's floppy,
	lea	(gd_bpb-gd_forward,a1),a3	; drive C a BPB and nothing more
	move.l	a3,(a2)+
	lea	(gd_rw-gd_forward,a1),a3
	move.l	a3,(a2)+
	lea	(gd_mediach-gd_forward,a1),a3
	move.l	a3,(a2)+
	move.l	(_drvbits).w,(a2)+		; the machine's drives, for GOS's Dsetdrv
	lea	(gd_bcbs-gd_forward,a1),a3
	move.l	a1,d1
	sub.l	#GD_BUFFERS,d1
	move.l	a3,(a2)+
	bsr.s	gd_list
	move.l	a3,(a2)+
	bsr.s	gd_list
	bra.w	x_gos

; Two free buffer control blocks at a3 (link, drive -1, type, record, dirty, the buffer d1), as
; PP's path makes them; a3 and d1 move on.
gd_list:
	lea	(20,a3),a4
	move.l	a4,(a3)+
	bsr.s	gd_bcb
	clr.l	(a3)+
gd_bcb:
	move.l	#$ffff0000,(a3)+
	clr.l	(a3)+
	clr.l	(a3)+
	move.l	d1,(a3)+
	add.l	#$2000,d1
	rts

; PP's info screen, then our lines in its free rows, as gos5_patch.s's.
gd_info:
	bsr.w	x_info
	pea	gd_patched(pc)
	move.w	#9,-(sp)			; Cconws
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#6,sp
	move.w	p_floppy(pc),d0
	beq.s	gd_info_end
	pea	gd_floppy(pc)
	move.w	#9,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#6,sp
gd_info_end:
	rts
gd_patched:
	dc.b	27,'Y',32+9,32+0,"Patched for GEMDRIVE HD by SidecarTridge",27,'H',0
gd_floppy:
	dc.b	27,'Y',32+11,32+3,"Insert any floppy disk in drive A",27,'H',0
	even

; GEMDRIVE's CMD_SET_SHARED_VAR (SHARED_VARIABLE_STACK, p_md_stack), as gos5_patch.s's. Z set when
; the RP holds the new stack.
md_move_stack:
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a1,-(sp)
	lea	md_stack_words(pc),a1
	move.l	p_md_stack(pc),d0
	move.w	d0,(a1)+			; low word first
	swap	d0
	move.w	d0,(a1)
	moveq	#4,d6
md_try:
	move.l	(md_seed).l,d2
	lea	md_token_words(pc),a1
	move.w	d2,(a1)+
	swap	d2
	move.w	d2,(a1)
	swap	d2
	lea	(md_cmd).l,a0
	move.w	#$abcd,d1			; CMD_MAGIC_NUMBER
	tst.b	(a0,d1.w)
	moveq	#0,d7				; the checksum: every word after the magic
	lea	md_words(pc),a1
	moveq	#(md_words_end-md_words)/2-1,d5
md_send:
	move.w	(a1)+,d1
	add.w	d1,d7
	tst.b	(a0,d1.w)
	dbf	d5,md_send
	tst.b	(a0,d7.w)
	move.l	#$6ffff,d5			; COMMAND_TIMEOUT
md_wait:
	cmp.l	(md_token).l,d2
	bne.s	md_not_yet
	cmp.l	(md_seed).l,d2			; the seed moved on: a real answer
	bne.s	md_answered
md_not_yet:
	subq.l	#1,d5
	bne.s	md_wait
	dbf	d6,md_try
md_answered:
	move.l	p_md_stack(pc),d0
	cmp.l	(md_stack_var).l,d0
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a1		; keeps the flags
	rts
md_words:
	dc.w	$0487,12			; CMD_SET_SHARED_VAR, the payload's bytes with the token's
md_token_words:
	dc.w	0,0
	dc.w	16+6,0				; SHARED_VARIABLE_STACK
md_stack_words:
	dc.w	0,0
md_words_end:

; Runs at p_run as GOS's TRAP #1, for GOS and for the game. The call is on the caller's stack: the
; supervisor stack past the exception frame (6 bytes on the 68000), or the user stack. Every
; register but d0 is given back, as GEMDOS does.
;   - Pexec 0 and 3: gd_exec, the program loaded through the machine into GOS's memory.
;   - The file functions and Dfree: to the machine's TRAP #1, as a copy of the call on this stack, changed
;     there (the caller's own stays as it was): a name (Dsetpath, Fcreate, Fopen, Fdelete, Fattrib,
;     Fsfirst) in gd_name, each part cut to 8.3 as GEMDOS reads it, without a dot it ends with; a
;     handle (Fclose, Fread, Fwrite, Fseek, Fdatime) the machine's for ours.
;   - Everything else, and a handle that is not ours (0 to 5, the standard ones): GOS's trap1
;     (Dsetdrv, Dgetdrv, Fsetdta, Fgetdta, the memory, the console, Pterm, Pexec 4 to 6).
; Our handles are GOS's numbers: the machine's handle of a file Fopen or Fcreate opens is kept in
; gd_handles and the call returns 6 and up, the lowest free, as GOS would. Games count on it: PP's
; adaptation of Operation Stealth puts back a snapshot of the game's variables in which its open
; file is handle 6. Fsfirst and Fsnext: Hatari fills the DTA of the process its TOS's p_run holds
; (gemdos.c), which under GOS holds a GOS variable unless that TOS is 1.04, whose p_run is GOS's:
; elsewhere GOS's current process goes there for the call (the Multidevice asks for the DTA with
; Fgetdta, through $84: GOS's). gd_exec's own calls come back through $84, here.
GD_HANDLES	equ	16
gd_forward:
	movem.l	d1-d2/a0-a2,-(sp)		; GEMDOS keeps every register but d0, and callers count
	btst	#5,(20,sp)			; on it (gd_exec among them)
	bne.s	gd_super
	move.l	usp,a1
	bra.s	gd_fn
gd_super:
	lea	(20+6,sp),a1
gd_fn:
	move.w	(a1),d0
	cmpi.w	#$4b,d0				; Pexec
	beq.w	gd_pexec
	lea	gd_functions(pc),a0
gd_next:
	move.b	(a0)+,d1
	beq.s	gd_to_gos
	cmp.b	d1,d0
	bne.s	gd_next
	clr.l	-(sp)				; p_run's place and value, when Fsfirst or Fsnext swaps it
	clr.l	-(sp)
	movem.l	(a1),d1-d2/a0			; the call, copied: 12 bytes, Fread's, the longest
	movem.l	d1-d2/a0,-(sp)
	movea.l	sp,a2
	moveq	#2,d1				; the handle's place
	cmpi.b	#$36,d0
	beq.s	gd_call				; Dfree: the drive's free space, as it is
	cmpi.b	#$3e,d0
	bcs.s	gd_named			; Dsetpath, Fcreate, Fopen
	cmpi.b	#$41,d0
	bcs.s	gd_handle			; Fclose, Fread, Fwrite
	beq.s	gd_named			; Fdelete
	cmpi.b	#$43,d0
	beq.s	gd_named			; Fattrib
	bcs.s	gd_handle6			; Fseek
	cmpi.b	#$4e,d0
	beq.s	gd_named			; Fsfirst
	cmpi.b	#$57,d0
	bne.s	gd_call				; Dgetpath, Fsnext
gd_handle6:
	moveq	#6,d1				; Fseek, Fdatime: after a long
gd_handle:
	move.w	(a2,d1.w),d2
	subq.w	#6,d2
	cmpi.w	#GD_HANDLES,d2
	bcc.s	gd_not_ours
	add.w	d2,d2
	lea	gd_handles(pc),a0
	move.w	(a0,d2.w),(a2,d1.w)		; the machine's
	bpl.s	gd_call
gd_not_ours:
	lea	(20,sp),sp
gd_to_gos:
	movem.l	(sp)+,d1-d2/a0-a2
	move.l	gd_gos(pc),-(sp)
	rts
gd_named:
	movea.l	(2,a1),a0
	bsr.w	gd_cut
	bcs.w	gd_bad_name
	lea	gd_name(pc),a0
	move.l	a0,(2,a2)
	cmpi.b	#$3d,d0				; Fopen for reading and writing: for reading. The
	bne.s	gd_call				; Multidevice's GEMDRIVE locks a file open for writing,
	cmpi.w	#2,(6,a2)			; and Noddy's Playtime opens data\driving.dat so, never
	bne.s	gd_call				; closes it and loads it again; no game writes through
	clr.w	(6,a2)				; such a handle (Fcreate makes the files they write)
gd_call:
	cmpi.b	#$4e,d0				; Fsfirst, Fsnext: the DTA
	bcs.s	gd_go
	cmpi.b	#$4f,d0
	bhi.s	gd_go
	move.l	gd_mach_run(pc),d1
	cmp.l	gd_gos_run(pc),d1
	beq.s	gd_go
	movea.l	d1,a0
	move.l	a0,(12,a2)
	move.l	(a0),(16,a2)
	movea.l	gd_gos_run(pc),a1
	move.l	(a1),(a0)			; GOS's current process, for the call
gd_go:
	pea	gd_back(pc)			; a supervisor's call: the copy past the frame
	move.w	sr,-(sp)
	move.l	gd_machine(pc),-(sp)
	rts
gd_back:
	movea.l	sp,a2
	move.l	(12,a2),d1
	beq.s	gd_back_fn
	movea.l	d1,a0
	move.l	(16,a2),(a0)			; p_run as it was
gd_back_fn:
	move.w	(a2),d1
	cmpi.w	#$3e,d1
	beq.s	gd_closed
	cmpi.w	#$3c,d1				; Fcreate, Fopen: the machine's handle kept, ours returned
	bcs.s	gd_end
	cmpi.w	#$3d,d1
	bhi.s	gd_end
	tst.l	d0
	bmi.s	gd_end
	lea	gd_handles(pc),a0
	moveq	#GD_HANDLES-1,d1
gd_free:
	tst.w	(a0)+
	dbmi	d1,gd_free
	bmi.s	gd_slot
	moveq	#-35,d0				; ENHNDL: no handle of ours left
	bra.s	gd_end
gd_slot:
	move.w	d0,-(a0)
	lea	gd_handles(pc),a1
	move.l	a0,d0
	sub.l	a1,d0
	lsr.l	#1,d0
	addq.l	#6,d0
	bra.s	gd_end
gd_closed:					; Fclose: its place free again
	move.w	(2,a2),d1
	lea	gd_handles(pc),a0
	moveq	#GD_HANDLES-1,d2
gd_find:
	cmp.w	(a0)+,d1
	dbeq	d2,gd_find
	bne.s	gd_end
	move.w	#-1,-(a0)
gd_end:
	lea	(20,sp),sp
	movem.l	(sp)+,d1-d2/a0-a2
	rte
gd_bad_name:
	moveq	#-33,d0				; EFILNF: an empty name, or one with no end, as GOS answers
	cmpi.w	#$3b,(a2)			; Dsetpath(""): the path as it is, and 0, as GOS
	bne.s	gd_end				; (Slightly Magic sets it before each file)
	moveq	#0,d0
	bra.s	gd_end

; The name at a0, cut to 8.3 into gd_name; carry set when it is empty or has no end within 255
; bytes: Hatari passes a call with an empty name to the GEMDOS it chains to, here the ROM's (Battle
; Probe opens ""), and an endless one would run past gd_name.
gd_cut:
	tst.b	(a0)
	bne.s	gd_cut_go
	ori	#1,ccr
	rts
gd_cut_go:
	move.l	a3,-(sp)
	lea	(255,a0),a3
	lea	gd_name(pc),a1
gd_part:
	move.l	a1,d2				; the part's first character
	moveq	#8,d1				; a part's name: 8 characters
gd_char:
	cmpa.l	a3,a0
	bcc.s	gd_too_long
	move.b	(a0)+,d0
	beq.s	gd_trim
	cmpi.b	#$5c,d0				; backslash
	beq.s	gd_trim
	cmpi.b	#'.',d0
	beq.s	gd_dot
	subq.w	#1,d1
	bmi.s	gd_char				; past 8.3: GEMDOS drops it
	move.b	d0,(a1)+
	bra.s	gd_char
gd_dot:
	move.b	d0,(a1)+
	moveq	#3,d1				; its extension: 3
	bra.s	gd_char
gd_trim:					; a part ends: a dot it ends with goes, as GEMDOS reads
	cmpa.l	d2,a1				; "RESIDENT." (Video Kid); not "." or ".."
	beq.s	gd_put
	cmpi.b	#'.',(-1,a1)
	bne.s	gd_put
	move.l	a1,d1
	subq.l	#1,d1
	cmp.l	d2,d1
	beq.s	gd_put
	cmpi.b	#'.',(-2,a1)
	beq.s	gd_put
	subq.l	#1,a1
gd_put:
	move.b	d0,(a1)+
	bne.s	gd_part				; a backslash: the next part
	movea.l	(sp)+,a3
	move.w	(a2),d0				; the function again; carry clear
	rts
gd_too_long:
	movea.l	(sp)+,a3
	ori	#1,ccr
	rts

; Pexec 0 (load and go) and 3 (load): GOS's Pexec would read the program through its own file
; code, by sectors. So: Fopen and Fread through the machine, GOS's Pexec 5 for the basepage and
; its TPA, the text and data read into it, relocated, the BSS cleared (and the rest of the TPA,
; unless the program's fastload bit is set, as TOS 1.04 does), the basepage filled in. Pexec 3
; returns the basepage; for Pexec 0 the caller's call is made Pexec 6 (the memory given to the
; program, as TOS 1.04's Pexec 0 does) and handed to GOS. Other modes: GOS's.
gd_pexec:
	move.w	(2,a1),d0
	beq.s	gd_exec
	cmpi.w	#3,d0
	bne.w	gd_to_gos
gd_exec:
	movem.l	d3-d7/a3-a6,-(sp)
	movea.l	a1,a5				; function, mode, name, command line, environment
	lea	(-28,sp),sp
	movea.l	sp,a4				; the program's header
	clr.w	-(sp)				; Fopen(name, 0)
	move.l	(4,a5),-(sp)
	move.w	#$3d,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#8,sp
	move.l	d0,d7
	bmi.w	gd_exec_end
	pea	(a4)				; Fread(handle, 28, header)
	pea	(28).w
	move.w	d7,-(sp)
	move.w	#$3f,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	lea	(12,sp),sp
	moveq	#-66,d3				; EPLFMT
	cmpi.l	#28,d0
	bne.w	gd_exec_close
	cmpi.w	#$601a,(a4)
	bne.w	gd_exec_close
	move.l	(12,a5),-(sp)			; Pexec(5, 0, command line, environment): GOS's
	move.l	(8,a5),-(sp)
	clr.l	-(sp)
	move.w	#5,-(sp)
	move.w	#$4b,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	lea	(16,sp),sp
	move.l	d0,d3
	bmi.w	gd_exec_close
	movea.l	d0,a6				; the basepage
	lea	(256,a6),a3			; the text's place
	move.l	(2,a4),d4			; text
	move.l	(6,a4),d5			; data
	move.l	(10,a4),d6			; BSS
	move.l	d4,d1
	add.l	d5,d1
	add.l	d6,d1
	move.l	(4,a6),d2			; p_hitpa
	sub.l	a3,d2
	moveq	#-39,d3				; ENSMEM
	cmp.l	d1,d2
	bcs.w	gd_exec_free
	move.l	a3,-(sp)			; Fread(handle, text + data, text's place)
	move.l	d4,d1
	add.l	d5,d1
	move.l	d1,-(sp)
	move.w	d7,-(sp)
	move.w	#$3f,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	lea	(12,sp),sp
	moveq	#-66,d3
	move.l	d4,d1
	add.l	d5,d1
	cmp.l	d1,d0
	bne.w	gd_exec_free
	lea	(a3,d1.l),a2			; the BSS's place
	tst.w	(26,a4)				; ph_absflag: no relocation
	bne.s	gd_exec_bss
	clr.w	-(sp)				; Fseek(28 + text + data + symbols, handle, 0)
	move.w	d7,-(sp)
	moveq	#28,d0
	add.l	d1,d0
	add.l	(14,a4),d0
	move.l	d0,-(sp)
	move.w	#$42,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	lea	(10,sp),sp
	move.l	a2,-(sp)			; Fread(handle, the TPA left, BSS's place): the fixups
	move.l	(4,a6),d0
	sub.l	a2,d0
	move.l	d0,-(sp)
	move.w	d7,-(sp)
	move.w	#$3f,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	lea	(12,sp),sp
	moveq	#4,d1
	cmp.l	d1,d0
	blt.s	gd_exec_bss			; none
	movea.l	a2,a0
	move.l	(a0)+,d1
	beq.s	gd_exec_bss
	lea	(a3,d1.l),a1
	move.l	a3,d2
	add.l	d2,(a1)
gd_fix:
	moveq	#0,d1
	move.b	(a0)+,d1
	beq.s	gd_exec_bss
	cmpi.b	#1,d1
	bne.s	gd_fix_at
	lea	(254,a1),a1
	bra.s	gd_fix
gd_fix_at:
	adda.l	d1,a1
	add.l	d2,(a1)
	bra.s	gd_fix
gd_exec_bss:
	move.l	(4,a6),d1			; up to p_hitpa, or the BSS alone with fastload
	sub.l	a2,d1
	btst	#0,(25,a4)			; ph_prgflags bit 0: fastload
	beq.s	gd_exec_clear
	move.l	d6,d1
gd_exec_clear:
	movea.l	a2,a0
	move.l	d1,d0
	lsr.l	#2,d0
	bra.s	gd_clear_next
gd_clear:
	clr.l	(a0)+
gd_clear_next:
	subq.l	#1,d0
	bpl.s	gd_clear
	andi.w	#3,d1
	bra.s	gd_clear_byte_next
gd_clear_byte:
	clr.b	(a0)+
gd_clear_byte_next:
	dbf	d1,gd_clear_byte
	move.l	a3,(8,a6)			; p_tbase, p_tlen, p_dbase, p_dlen, p_bbase, p_blen
	move.l	d4,(12,a6)
	lea	(a3,d4.l),a0
	move.l	a0,(16,a6)
	move.l	d5,(20,a6)
	move.l	a2,(24,a6)
	move.l	d6,(28,a6)
	move.w	d7,-(sp)			; Fclose(handle)
	move.w	#$3e,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#4,sp
	move.l	a6,d0
	tst.w	(2,a5)
	bne.s	gd_exec_end			; Pexec 3: the basepage
	move.w	#6,(2,a5)			; Pexec 0: the caller's own call becomes Pexec(6, 0,
	clr.l	(4,a5)				; basepage, 0), and goes to GOS as the caller made it,
	move.l	a6,(8,a5)			; its frame on the caller's stack: GOS keeps the
	clr.l	(12,a5)				; caller's context there while the program runs, as
	lea	(28,sp),sp			; for its own Pexec 0 (a call from here kept it on the
	movem.l	(sp)+,d3-d7/a3-a6		; supervisor stack, which the program then overwrote:
	bra.w	gd_to_gos			; Erik's intro returned through garbage)
gd_exec_free:
	move.l	(44,a6),-(sp)			; Mfree its environment and basepage
	move.w	#$49,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#6,sp
	move.l	a6,-(sp)
	move.w	#$49,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#6,sp
gd_exec_close:
	move.w	d7,-(sp)			; Fclose(handle), the error in d3
	move.w	#$3e,-(sp)
	trap	#1
	addq.l	#4,sp
	move.l	d3,d0
gd_exec_end:
	lea	(28,sp),sp
	movem.l	(sp)+,d3-d7/a3-a6
	movem.l	(sp)+,d1-d2/a0-a2
	rte

; The driver GOS takes: drives A and B go to GOS's own floppy routines, as PP's path has them;
; drive C has a BPB, so that a game that asks for it before its files (Getbpb(2): Starblade,
; Windsurf Willy, as the Silmarils games of solutions.md 3.2) goes on to read them by name;
; it is never changed, and its sectors fail.
gd_bpb:
	cmpi.w	#2,(4,sp)
	bcc.s	gd_bpb_c
	move.l	gd_flop(pc),-(sp)
	bne.s	gd_chain
	addq.l	#4,sp
	moveq	#0,d0				; no floppy routine: no BPB
	rts
gd_bpb_c:
	lea	gd_bpb_data(pc),a0
	move.l	a0,d0
	rts
gd_rw:
	cmpi.w	#2,(14,sp)			; rwflag, buffer, count, record, drive
	bcc.s	gd_fail
	move.l	gd_flop+4(pc),-(sp)
	bne.s	gd_chain
	addq.l	#4,sp
gd_fail:
	moveq	#-1,d0
	rts
gd_mediach:
	cmpi.w	#2,(4,sp)
	bcc.s	gd_not_changed
	move.l	gd_flop+8(pc),-(sp)
	bne.s	gd_chain
	addq.l	#4,sp
	moveq	#-1,d0
	rts
gd_not_changed:
	moveq	#0,d0
	rts
gd_chain:
	rts					; to the routine pushed
gd_flop:
	dc.l	0,0,0				; GOS's hdv_bpb, hdv_rw, hdv_mediach for drives A and B
gd_bpb_data:					; FAT16, 512-byte records, 1 KB clusters
	dc.w	512,2,1024,32,128,129,289,32000,1
gd_machine:
	dc.l	0
gd_gos:
	dc.l	0
gd_mach_run:
	dc.l	0				; the machine's p_run
gd_gos_run:
	dc.l	0				; GOS's
; Dfree, Dsetpath, Fcreate, Fopen, Fclose, Fread, Fwrite, Fdelete, Fseek, Fattrib, Dgetpath,
; Fsfirst, Fsnext, Fdatime
gd_functions:
	dc.b	$36,$3b,$3c,$3d,$3e,$3f,$40,$41,$42,$43,$47,$4e,$4f,$57,0
	even
gd_handles:
	dcb.w	GD_HANDLES,-1			; the machine's handle of each of ours, -1 when free
gd_bcbs:
	dcb.b	4*20,0				; the two lists' buffer control blocks
gd_name:
	dcb.b	256,0				; a name cut to 8.3
gd_forward_end:
patch_end:

atomoutput-svinjoland-analysis-reverse-e.text:
# Svinjoland reverse-engineering handoff

## Result

The three supplied files are 16-bit DOS MZ programs compiled to native x86 with
Microsoft QuickBASIC and compressed with Microsoft EXEPACK. They are not Windows
PE executables. The EXEPACK layer has been removed without modifying the
originals, the game-owned QuickBASIC modules have been separated from the
runtime, and their reachable code, literals, literal references, and direct
compare/jump sites have been exported.

| Game | Packed bytes | Unpacked bytes | Unpacked relocations | Game code range | Literals | Literal references | Direct compare/jump sites |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Svinjoland | 70,682 | 75,536 | 1,116 | `0x0030..0x52e2` | 341 | 637 | 33 |
| Svinjoland 2 | 109,734 | 143,792 | 2,170 | `0x0030..0xbc12` | 511 | 1,305 | 24 |
| Svinjoland 3 | 110,008 | 140,288 | 3,315 | `0x0030..0x9322` | 374 | 714 | 16 |

“Direct compare/jump sites” does not include the many command decisions made by
calling the QuickBASIC string-comparison routine and then branching on its
result. Those calls and their command literals are annotated in the assembly
exports.

## Chain of custody

The supplied files remain untouched.

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `Svinja/SVINJA.EXE` | `2bb0bf31b33da8b8f321de218c35e5e1d9b7872dbe3a74d0c29c798d463b4dc3` |
| `Svinja2/SVINJA2.EXE` | `abf9f12fbd471fa0ae5ba688109b843170b3964090cf09173c85846ea0f0b63c` |
| `Svinja3/Svinja3.exe` | `4cbd4842becae5f9577e27ae3a14581e8bc113c66c93fc561abe370667bd14bf` |

The unpacked analysis copies are:

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `analysis/unpacked/SVINJA.EXE` | `e4c56a3406065c824c4215dee1029d1c96f92669cefca96fa9548d364f96228f` |
| `analysis/unpacked/SVINJA2.EXE` | `fa8003adf14d143ef1a8c92149294a9a12f6228c1da60a939b6a22275b478211` |
| `analysis/unpacked/SVINJA3.EXE` | `ee4b73edce502e6ff1ed45bafd18561ea373f25a1d0186bd0021e705a4aad1f2` |
| `analysis/unpacked/CREDITS.EXE` | `5e245d34d45581ca6b92a85a553e9ef11b5cab6939cfd85b79d989d91cf567c6` |

The files were unpacked with `w4kfu/unEXEPACK` at commit
`db26f9e2d23af37e6508436b62cb98cbbb86a275`. Its decoded `RB` header values
restore the programs' original entry points, stacks, image sizes, and relocation
tables.

The complete release was subsequently recovered from the Internet Archive item
[Svinjolend triologija](https://archive.org/details/svinja-3) into
`archive_original/Svinjoland/`. All 40 files in the archived `Svinjoland` tree
match the MD5 values in `analysis/archive_metadata.json`; the three archived
executables also match the originally supplied executables byte for byte.

Format/tool references: [w4kfu/unEXEPACK source and format notes](https://github.com/w4kfu/unEXEPACK),
[David Fifield's EXEPACK implementation and stub documentation](https://www.bamsoftware.com/software/exepack/),
and the archived [Microsoft EXEPACK documentation](https://msarchive.pcjs.org/mspl13/msdos/encyclopedia/section4/).

## Recovered behavior

### Svinjoland

The first game identifies itself as “THE ULTIMATE SERBIAN QBASIC TEXT-BASED
ADVENTURE by TABA.” It is a mostly linear, numbered-choice adventure. The intro
explicitly says that choices are numbers 1 through 3 and that only one path is
correct. The code reads a numeric answer and compares it with `1`, `2`, and `3`,
with bad values looping or reaching death text. It asks for the player's name,
uses it in later output, contains chapters and an epilogue, and renders its logo
and borders entirely as embedded CP437 text.

The two dominant literal consumers are:

- `0x02db:0x4342`: print a literal followed by normal line handling (580 uses,
  including the shared empty-string descriptor used for blank lines).
- `0x02db:0x433d`: print/compose a literal without the same line handling (15 uses).

The complete narrative is recoverable from `svinja.json`; `svinja.asm` preserves
the exact ordering, decisions, delays, screen/color calls, and text uses.

### Svinjoland 2 — Nightmare Continues

The second game is a command-parser adventure dated 21 May 1999. It starts in
the player's room, accepts commands and synonyms such as `UZMI ORMAN`,
`ISPITAJ RADIO`, `ZAPAD`, `IDI NA ZAPAD`, `PRICAJ SA PRODAVCEM`, `RESTART`,
`KRAJ`, and `IZLAZ`, and later moves through an alley and butcher shop toward a
confrontation with the neighbour. The game requires uppercase input by telling
the player to enable Caps Lock; the rewrite should normalize case instead.

Important runtime anchors are:

- `0x0650:0x236c`: text/ASCII-art output (917 annotated uses, including blank
  lines through the shared empty-string descriptor).
- `0x0650:0x27e6`: exact string comparison used by the command parser (331 uses).
- `0x0650:0x0a81`: DOS shell command; used to rename `sl2.sys` to `DA.GIF` and
  restore the name later.

`ime.dat` is opened in two modes around game-code offsets `0x18c7` and `0x197c`;
the surrounding logic indicates it is used to persist and reload the player
name/state.

### Svinjoland 3

The third game keeps the command-parser design and expands it into room-based
navigation. The recovered commands include movement (`SEVER`, `ISTOK`, `ZAPAD`,
`JUG` and `IDI NA ...`), global actions (`UZMI`, `ISPITAJ`, `PRICAJ`, `RESTART`,
`IZLAZ`, `KRAJ`, `POGLEDAJ OKO SEBE`), and many room-specific synonyms. The
recovered areas include the bedroom, lift/building, outside/park/bridge, cafe,
toilet, container area, and an in-game “Svinjoland Operating System” sequence.

Important runtime anchors are:

- `0x071d:0x20b6`: narrative/UI output (267 annotated uses).
- `0x071d:0x2530`: exact command comparison (309 uses, including comparisons
  against the shared empty-string descriptor).
- `0x071d:0x0be2`: strongly inferred QuickBASIC binary graphics load; every
  annotated argument is a room-art `.DAT` name (93 uses).
- `0x071d:0x0cb5`: DOS shell command. It changes to the `SVINJA3` directory and
  temporarily renames `Credits.dat` to `Credits.exe` for execution.

The complete winning path is now resolved. The puzzle chain is knowledge-only:
`ISPITAJ PATIKU` reveals `19799`; entering that below the park bench reveals
`DACETEMIKIWONAMAMAKA`; that password admits the player to the cafe; examining
the toilet bowl finds the missing magazines. The final handler at `0x59c2`
shows the victory text, loads `KR1.DAT` through `KR5.DAT`, runs the separate
credits executable, and terminates at runtime exit call `0x071d:0x2045`.
There are no gameplay inventory/prerequisite variables: the direct writes at
`0x5b01` and `0x5b0c` occur only after victory while setting up the finale.

## Recovered external files and formats

The original external files are no longer missing. They reveal that the third
game's “graphics” are colored DOS text screens, not opaque bitmap resources:

- Svinjoland 2's `SL2.SYS` is an intact 320x200 GIF89a intro image. The code's
  rename to `DA.GIF` is only an extension disguise. `IME.DAT` contains the
  initial name `ACA` followed by CR/LF, confirming it as the player-name file.
- Svinjoland 3's `pigzl.dat` is another intact 320x200 GIF89a image.
- Each of the 25 uppercase Svinjoland 3 `.DAT` scene files is 4,015 bytes: a
  QuickBASIC `BSAVE` header for `B800:0000`, exactly 4,000 bytes of 80x25 color
  text video memory, then a repeated header and DOS EOF byte. Every two-byte
  cell contains the original CP437 character and VGA color/blink attribute.
- `Credits.dat` is the recovered separate DOS MZ credits program. It is only
  1,138 bytes and is compressed with aPack; Svinjoland 3 temporarily renames it
  to `Credits.exe` before running it. Its embedded depacker has been emulated at
  two load addresses to reconstruct a normal 2,974-byte MZ with one relocation,
  entry `0000:07AE`, and stack `00B8:0200`.
- The remaining recovered material includes all three Windows icons, DOS PIF
  launch descriptors, both text readmes, and Svinjoland 3 installer-project data
  in `irunin.dat`. That installer data states that the original game expected
  `C:\SVINJA3`, which explains its hard-coded directory change.

`analysis/tools/decode_bsave_text.py` converts every saved text screen to three
forms: an exact 80x25 Unicode/CP437 text grid, ANSI color text, and a 720x400 PNG
preview. The grid and attribute interpretation are lossless. PNG previews use
The previews now use the monochrome IBM VGA 8×16 CP437 bitmap strike, rendered
as exact 9×16 VGA text cells. Codes C0-DF receive the hardware-compatible
ninth-column duplication used to join box-drawing characters; no antialiasing
or outline-font substitution is involved.

### Reconstructed artwork for games 1 and 2

The first two executables contain narrative text and a recovered Svinjoland 2
intro GIF, but no location-screen files comparable to Svinjoland 3's 4,000-byte
BSAVE buffers. New scene illustrations live under
`analysis/assets/svinja/screens/` and `analysis/assets/svinja2/screens/`. They
are AI-concept-guided compositions rebuilt as deterministic 80x25 CP437 text
buffers by `analysis/tools/build_reconstructed_screens.py`. They are not
original assets and are labeled as reconstructed throughout the rewrite data
and browser interface. The concept sheets used as visual briefs are preserved
under `analysis/concepts/`.

### Separate credits animation

The unpacked credits are a small handwritten VGA mode 13h animation, not another
QuickBASIC module. It obtains the BIOS 8x8 font with `INT 10h, AX=1130h`, installs
a 256-color palette, renders into a 64,000-byte off-screen buffer, adds a
pseudorandom star field, applies a three-pass four-neighbour blur, draws seven
credit phases, copies the buffer to `A000:0000`, fades the 768 DAC values over 64
frames, restores text mode 3, and exits through `INT 21h, AH=4Ch`.

The exact recovered credit text is: “CREDITS”, “Created by: TABA and BioHazard”,
“Programmed by: TABA”, “Scenario by: TABA and BioHazard”, “Graphics by: TZN”,
and “I svim ostalima koji su pomogli stvaranje ove bolesne igre... FALA :)”.
Representative emulated frames and fade stages are in
`analysis/assets/svinja3/credits/`.

## Analysis artifacts

- `svinja.json`, `svinja2.json`, `svinja3.json`: machine-readable MZ/module
  metadata, every recovered CP437 literal decoded to Unicode, exact descriptor
  and file offsets, all literal load sites, nearby runtime calls, and direct
  branch candidates.
- `svinja.asm`, `svinja2.asm`, `svinja3.asm`: recursively decoded game-module
  assembly. Runtime-library bodies are excluded. Literal text is attached as a
  comment at every use site.
- `unpacked/`: relocation-restored executables suitable for Ghidra's “Old-style
  DOS Executable (MZ)” loader (`x86:LE:16:Real Mode`).
- `tools/extract_quickbasic.py`: reproducible extractor/listing generator.
- `archive_metadata.json`: Internet Archive provenance and published hashes.
- `assets/svinja3/screens/`: decoded `.txt`, `.ansi`, and `.png` versions of all
  25 scene screens, plus `manifest.json` and a visual `contact-sheet.png`.
- `unpacked/CREDITS.EXE`: relocation-restored conventional MZ for the separate
  aPack-compressed credits program.
- `assets/svinja3/credits/`: 12 emulated VGA frames covering every credits phase
  and palette fade, with a manifest and contact sheet.
- `assets/svinja2/intro.gif` and `assets/svinja3/pigzl.gif`: byte-identical copies
  of the disguised GIFs under useful extensions.
- `assets/svinja*/icon.ico` and `icon.png`: preserved icons and PNG previews.
- `tools/unpack_apack_credits.py` and `tools/capture_credits.py`: safe CPU-emulated
  credits unpacking and framebuffer capture; DOS code is never run as host code.

Example regeneration command:

```sh
python3 analysis/tools/extract_quickbasic.py \
  analysis/unpacked/SVINJA3.EXE \
  -o analysis/svinja3.json \
  -a analysis/svinja3.asm

python3 analysis/tools/decode_bsave_text.py \
  archive_original/Svinjoland/Svinja3/*.DAT \
  -o analysis/assets/svinja3/screens

python3 analysis/tools/unpack_apack_credits.py \
  archive_original/Svinjoland/Svinja3/Credits.dat \
  analysis/unpacked/CREDITS.EXE

python3 analysis/tools/capture_credits.py \
  analysis/unpacked/CREDITS.EXE \
  -o analysis/assets/svinja3/credits
```

The extractor uses a structural invariant rather than Serbian-language guesses:
for every genuine QuickBASIC literal, `file_offset_of_text - near_pointer` is
constant inside the module's DGROUP. The recovered bases are `0xcb60`, `0x16990`,
and `0x184d0` respectively.

## Recommended rewrite boundary

Use one small, data-driven adventure engine with two interaction modes:

1. A numbered-choice node runner for the first game.
2. A room/command rule engine for games two and three.

Keep content outside engine code. A practical schema needs rooms/nodes, displayed
paragraph IDs, accepted command aliases, prerequisites, inventory/state changes,
next room/node, death/ending outcomes, optional sound cues, and optional art IDs.
Preserve the recovered original text as one locale and add edited Serbian and
other translations separately. Normalize whitespace and input case only in the
engine; retain the raw strings in the preservation dataset.

The first implementation milestone should reproduce every original transition
using the recovered text and art. Modern graphics, audio, accessibility, save
games, and rewritten prose can then be layered on without changing the verified
game graph. Preserve source asset filenames as IDs, but make path handling
case-insensitive because DOS treated `IZLAZ.DAT` and `izlaz.dat` equivalently.

## Confidence and remaining work

- High confidence: file format, EXEPACK decoding, QuickBASIC identification,
  literal bytes, literal/code references, command vocabulary, external-file
  references, all recovered distribution hashes, and the 25 screen formats.
- Medium/high confidence: runtime-call roles inferred from arguments and repeated
  use patterns. The output and comparison calls are especially clear.
- The explicit room/node graphs and a tested Svinjoland 3 winning playthrough
  now exist under `rewrite/`. Remaining behavior-identical work is primarily
  timing, sound, startup/name persistence, exact rendering, and live comparison
  against the DOS originals—not missing story content or unresolved navigation.

# Svinjoland rewrite data

This directory is the engine-neutral preservation layer recovered from the three original DOS executables. It is intended to be consumed by a new engine without copying executable code.

## What is ready

| Game | Recovered model | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Svinjoland | 11 numbered-choice nodes, 33 options | 22 death outcomes, 10 continuations, 1 ending |
| Svinjoland 2 | 16 parser scenes, 118 semantic actions, 257 command aliases | All 331 string comparisons accounted for |
| Svinjoland 3 | 11 parser scenes, 86 semantic actions, 187 command aliases | All 309 string comparisons accounted for |

The parser datasets group spelling/synonym aliases by their exact original machine-code destination. They also preserve comparison offsets, handler offsets, locally referenced narrative text, restart/quit behavior, scene art filenames, death/replay prompts, numeric dialogue branches, and password comparisons.

Svinjoland 3's complete executable-backed winning path is represented, including its two-code knowledge chain, toilet-bowl ending handler, five `KR` finale screens, and recovered credits animation frames. The game does not maintain inventory flags for these puzzles; knowing and entering the codes is the original prerequisite.

The `behavior` field means:

- `stay`: handler returns to the same scene.
- `transition`: handler reaches one other named scene.
- `restart` or `quit`: global parser command.
- `game_over_interaction`: death sequence followed by the original D/N replay prompt.
- `nested_interaction`: a numeric choice, password, or other subprompt.
- `ending`: successful ending/credits path.

`reachable_scenes` is control-flow evidence, not a replacement for the exact handler. `evidence_literals` is deliberately local to the handler block so unrelated intro or runtime strings do not leak into an action.

## Files

- `games/svinja.json`, `games/svinja2.json`, and `games/svinja3.json`: recovered content and behavior.
- `games/manifest.json`: generated file hashes and validation result.
- `schema/game.schema.json`: shared JSON Schema contract.
- `../analysis/tools/build_rewrite_data.py`: reproducible extractor and validator.
- `../analysis/REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md`: executable, asset, toolchain, and provenance report.

Regenerate the datasets from the annotated disassemblies with:

```sh
python3 analysis/tools/build_rewrite_data.py --root . -o rewrite/games
```

The generator checks graph references, three-option choice nodes, unique scene IDs, nonempty command groups, and complete comparison accounting. A successful run rewrites the manifest with SHA-256 hashes.

## Playable browser build

`web/` contains a dependency-free reference engine and responsive interface. It runs all three games directly from the generated JSON, presents the recovered Svinjoland 2 scene narratives and Svinjoland 3 artwork, accepts parser commands without the original CAPS LOCK requirement, and implements the recovered numeric, password, death/replay, restart, quit, and ending flows.

Its presentation follows the games' original cultural and technical setting: the surrounding interface is entirely in Serbian, using a late-1990s Windows desktop/launcher and a DOS-style game console. Original dialogue, spellings, slang, and recovered VGA artwork remain unedited.

Svinjoland 1 and 2 did not contain location artwork equivalent to Svinjoland 3's
BSAVE screens. The browser build therefore includes newly reconstructed 80x25
CP437/VGA illustrations based on the executable-derived Serbian scene text and
visible objects. These screens are labeled `NOVA REKONSTRUISANA GRAFIKA` during
play and carry explicit `art_provenance` metadata; Svinjoland 3's recovered
screens remain labeled `ORIGINALNA GRAFIKA`.

Regenerate the reconstructed illustrations with:

```sh
python3 analysis/tools/build_reconstructed_screens.py --root .
```

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Then open `http://localhost:8080/rewrite/web/`. Run its automated tests with:

```sh
node --test rewrite/web/engine.test.mjs
```

## Preserved parser edge case

Svinjoland 2 compares `IDI U MESARU` and `UDJI U MESARU` twice in `junction_after_shop`, routing the first copies to the butcher and the later copies to the shop. Nothing mutates the input between those comparisons, so the first match always wins and the later pair is unreachable. The data records this with `duplicate_aliases`, `duplicate_alias_semantics`, and per-action `shadowed_aliases`. A faithful rewrite should route these phrases to the butcher; a compatibility/debug mode may expose the dead handler for study.

The scene labels are human-readable inferences. Offsets, strings, aliases, comparison totals, and dispatch destinations are the mechanically recovered facts. Text remains in its original Serbian/ASCII form so localization and editorial updates can be layered on top without damaging the preservation source.

# Matching decompilation

Separately from the recompiler, `games/<game>/decomp/src/` holds the games' source code,
recovered function by function: C (and a few assembly modules) that Borland C++ (3.0, 3.1
or 4.02, as each game was built) compiles, and TLINK links with the stock Borland runtime
and overlay manager, back into a DOS executable **byte-identical** to the original. The
build runs the DOS tools headless in DOSBox-X and compares the result with your copy of
the executable, which is not in the repository. See [docs/matching.md](docs/matching.md)
for the toolchain, the workflow and the techniques.

## Building

```bash
make -C games/cm1/decomp             # compile, relink, compare with the original
make -C games/cm1/decomp progress    # how much is done
```

The other games build the same way from `games/<game>/decomp`.

## Progress

| Game | Functions | Bytes | Not matched yet |
|---|---|---|---|
| Championship Manager (1992) | 723 / 723 | 300,349 / 300,349 (100%) | — |
| Championship Manager 93 | 816 / 816 | 368,424 / 368,424 (100%) | — |
| Championship Manager Italia | 817 / 817 | 374,470 / 374,470 (100%) | — |
| Championship Manager 94 (End of Season) | 855 / 855 | 371,750 / 371,750 (100%) | — |
| Championship Manager Italia 95 | 857 / 857 | 366,493 / 366,493 (100%) | — |

All five games are fully decompiled: every module is linked from its C (or assembly) source
and the executables are byte-identical. The last function in each of the first three was
the same one, ported from game to game: the menu of actions on one of your own players.
Several of its branches end with identical code, and BCC merges them into a different copy
from the one the original keeps, until the game is compiled with `-y` (line numbers in the
objects, which change that choice without leaving anything in the executable). CM94, built
with Borland C++ 4.02, matches it with code-free statements naming a variable
(`9007:511f`). See [docs/matching.md](docs/matching.md) on merged tails.

## Native ports

`games/cm1/port/`, `games/cm93/port/`, `games/cmese/port/`, `games/cmitalia/port/` and
`games/cmita95/port/` build CM1's, CM93's, CM94's, CM Italia's and CM Italia 95's decompiled sources as native Linux programs
with SDL3 (meson). Each works from a
converted copy and leaves `decomp/src/` as it is. All run on the same platform layer, `port/`, which replaces DOS,
the BIOS, the VGA card, the mouse and the games' assembly modules. See
[port/README.md](port/README.md), and the games' READMEs
([CM1](games/cm1/port/README.md), [CM93](games/cm93/port/README.md),
[CM94](games/cmese/port/README.md), [Italia](games/cmitalia/port/README.md), [Italia 95](games/cmita95/port/README.md)).

## Repository layout

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `games/<game>/decomp/` | The matching decompilation: `src/` (the C and assembly sources), makefile, symbols |
| `tools/match/` | The decompilation's tools: relink, per-function compare, diff, porting between games |
| `games/<game>/port/` | A game's native port (CM1, CM93, CM94, Italia, Italia 95): its converted sources and build |
| `port/`, `tools/port/` | The ports' shared platform layer, and their conversion tools |
| `docs/matching.md` | Toolchain, workflow and techniques |

## Legal

The sources in `games/*/decomp/src/` reproduce the games' program code, and the rights in
it belong to the games' owners. See the [README](README.md#legal).

# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(gravity VERSION 1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

option(GRAV_SINGLE_PRECISION "Single precision variables like QuickBASIC (bit-faithful results)" ON)

find_package(SDL2 REQUIRED)

add_executable(grav WIN32
  src/main.cpp
  src/qb.cpp
  src/grav.cpp
  src/help.cpp
  src/klok.cpp)

if(TARGET SDL2::SDL2main)
  target_link_libraries(grav PRIVATE SDL2::SDL2main)
endif()
if(TARGET SDL2::SDL2)
  target_link_libraries(grav PRIVATE SDL2::SDL2)
else()
  target_include_directories(grav PRIVATE ${SDL2_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  target_link_libraries(grav PRIVATE ${SDL2_LIBRARIES})
endif()

if(GRAV_SINGLE_PRECISION)
  target_compile_definitions(grav PRIVATE GRAV_SINGLE)
endif()
if(MINGW)
  target_link_options(grav PRIVATE -s -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++ -Wl,-Bstatic,--whole-archive -lwinpthread -Wl,--no-whole-archive)
endif()
if(WIN32 AND TARGET SDL2::SDL2)
  # put SDL2.dll next to grav.exe
  add_custom_command(TARGET grav POST_BUILD
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different $<TARGET_FILE:SDL2::SDL2> $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:grav>)
  install(FILES $<TARGET_FILE:SDL2::SDL2> DESTINATION .)
endif()
if(MSVC)
  target_compile_definitions(grav PRIVATE _USE_MATH_DEFINES _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS)
  target_compile_options(grav PRIVATE /W3 /utf-8)
else()
  target_compile_options(grav PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
endif()

# copy the program data next to the executable
add_custom_command(TARGET grav POST_BUILD
  COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_directory ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/dist $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:grav>)

install(TARGETS grav RUNTIME DESTINATION .)
install(DIRECTORY dist/ DESTINATION .)
